anomalies.observed: R6 (10K) is drawn as a pull-up from the TACH net to the raw VCC rail (the LM1117 input rail), while the ATtiny tach input sits in the regulated +5V domain.
anomalies.expected: The fan tach open-collector pull-up should return to the MCU's +5V rail, not to the unregulated VCC rail, so the MCU input is not exposed to the fan supply voltage.

evidence.quote: R6 10K, top terminal on VCC and bottom terminal on TACH (sheet /, fan_controller.kicad_sch)
U2 ATtiny45-20P pin 8 (VCC) tied to +5V; U3 ATtiny13V-10S pin 8 tied to +5V (sheet /, fan_controller.kicad_sch)

anomalies.impact: Since the LM1117-5.0 requires VCC well above 5V (the board is powered from the fan/12V rail and VCC_OUT feeds the fan), the TACH line idles at VCC rather than 5V, over-stressing/over-volting the ATtiny tach input and potentially damaging it.

anomalies.observed: C1 is a 100pF capacitor sitting on the power rail next to C2 (100nF), in the regulator/MCU decoupling area.
anomalies.expected: A power-rail bypass/decoupling capacitor in this position should be around 100nF; if this is the LM1117 output capacitor it should be at least ~10µF per the regulator's stability requirement.
anomalies.impact: A 100pF cap provides essentially no bulk/bypass, leaving the 5V rail (or the regulator loop) poorly decoupled and potentially unstable, so the MCU rail could be noisy or oscillate.

anomalies.observed: The two alternative ATtiny footprints do not map the same signal to the same pin: U2 (ATtiny45) puts TACH on pin 2 (PB3) and POT on pin 3 (PB4), while U3 (ATtiny13) puts POT on pin 2 (PB3) and TACH on pin 3 (PB4).
anomalies.expected: Two drop-in alternative 8-pin ATtiny footprints sharing the same nets should assign the same net to the same pin (both ATtiny45 and ATtiny13 have PB3 = pin 2, PB4 = pin 3), so the same firmware/board behaviour applies regardless of which MCU is populated.

evidence.quote: U2 ATtiny45-20P: pin 2 TACH, pin 3 POT (sheet /, fan_controller.kicad_sch)
U3 ATtiny13V-10S: pin 2 POT, pin 3 TACH (sheet /, fan_controller.kicad_sch)

anomalies.impact: The POT (analog setpoint) and TACH (fan-speed feedback) functions land on different MCU pins depending on which footprint is populated, so firmware written for one variant reads/senses the wrong pin on the other and the fan control/tachometry behaves incorrectly.

parsed.summary: The schematic contains likely deviations from a correctly functioning 5V ATtiny fan controller: the TACH pull-up R6 returns to the raw VCC rail instead of +5V (exposing the MCU input to the fan supply), the bypass capacitor C1 is 100pF where ~100nF is required, and the two alternative ATtiny footprints assign POT/TACH to opposite pins.
